<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is safe to process with `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. 

The file contains standard Arch packaging code with no dangerous patterns. The `pkgver` variable is hardcoded to `0.1.3` (no `pkgver()` function that would execute during sourcing). The `source` arrays reference the upstream GitHub releases page (`${_ghurl}/releases/download/${_gitversion}/...`) which is the package's own distribution point - expected and legitimate for a `-bin` package. Both `sha256sums_x86_64` and `sha256sums_aarch64` are provided with actual checksums (not `SKIP`), so verification is possible. The `::` syntax in source entries is standard makepkg notation for specifying remote URLs. The `_ghurlraw` variable is defined but not used in any source entry, and even if it were, raw.githubusercontent.com is the official GitHub content host. The `package()` function and all its commands (cd, install) are out of scope since `--nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` prevents their execution. No `eval`, no `curl|bash`, no base64-encoded commands, no data exfiltration, and no reverse shells are present. The code is consistent with ordinary AUR packaging practices for a prebuilt binary package.

While this PKGBUILD will be audited more comprehensively later (including `prepare()`, `build()`, `package()` phases), the narrow safety gate of fetching sources and parsing the PKGBUILD is clean.
</details>
<evidence>
